title: PhlimboV3 and MigratorV2V3 are deployed to mainnet from `via_ir = true` bytecode that no phlimbo-ea test has ever exercised, and story 076's Preflight ticks a `via_ir off` premise this repo does not have
originBasis: Exact fingerprint c544c9f6… absent. Independent sweep: NO ledger entry names foundry.toml, via_ir, or any build-configuration root cause. Cross-repo phlimbo-ea V3-L-19 (38aefbfb…) is in a DIFFERENT project ledger and is outside this ledger's fingerprint space — see suppressionsExplicitlyDeclined. NEW.
specConformanceDeviation: A ticked Preflight item certifies a build profile this repository does not have.
specConformanceStoryText: Story 076 Implementation Notes, line 382: 'Per house knowledge, phlimbo builds use legacy + optimizer with `via_ir` OFF'. Preflight, line 538, TICKED: '[x] Confirm `forge build` succeeds with `PhlimboV3` and `MigratorV2V3` imported via the existing `@phlimbo-ea/` remapping, and that `PhlimboV3` lands under the EIP-170 24 KB limit in this repo's profile (optimizer on, `via_ir` off).' phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml:1-7 sets via_ir = true.
description: `phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml:1-7` sets `optimizer = true`, `optimizer_runs = 10000`, `via_ir = true`. `lib/phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:6-15` sets `via_ir = false` with an in-file comment explaining that via_ir caches `block.timestamp` and breaks repeated `vm.warp`. Every phlimbo-ea test and every audit of PhlimboV3/MigratorV2V3 (stories 022-031, audits phlimbo-ea-07..11) therefore validated legacy-pipeline bytecode. Story 076's Phase 4e is the code that actually CREATEs both contracts on mainnet, and it compiles them under phStaging2's via_ir pipeline. Story 076's Implementation Notes assert "Per house knowledge, phlimbo builds use legacy + optimizer with `via_ir` OFF", and its Preflight checklist ticks `[x] ... that PhlimboV3 lands under the EIP-170 24 KB limit in this repo's profile (optimizer on, `via_ir` off)`. This repo's profile is via_ir ON. The EIP-170 purpose of that criterion is satisfied (PhlimboV3 measures 14,529 B here, 10,047 B of margin, `forge build --sizes`), so nothing is blocked — but the tick was recorded against a build profile that does not exist in this repository.
impact: Not an exploit and no defect is demonstrated — via_ir and legacy are both supported solc pipelines. What is demonstrated is an assurance gap at the deploy site: the artifact that will hold user principal is not the artifact the audit and test suites exercised, and the story's own preflight records the opposite. This is a deploy-gate/QA-class issue, not a vulnerability, and its severity should not exceed what that supports.
evidence: foundry.toml:1-7 (this repo) vs lib/phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:6-15; `forge build --sizes` in workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging reports PhlimboV3 14,529 B / margin 10,047 B, MigratorV2V3 8,248 B. Story 076 Implementation Notes and Preflight checklist item as quoted.
recommendation: Either (a) run phlimbo-ea's PhlimboV3/MigratorV2V3 suites once under `FOUNDRY_PROFILE` with `via_ir = true` and record the result, accepting the documented `vm.warp`/`block.timestamp` caveat by adjusting only the affected tests, or (b) set `via_ir = false` for this repo's build of the phlimbo-ea sources — phlimbo-ea ledger entry V3-L-19 records the measured fact that the legacy build is 15,979 B with 8,597 B of EIP-170 margin, so via_ir is NOT load-bearing for the size limit and can be dropped freely. Independently, correct story 076's Implementation Notes and Preflight tick to say `via_ir` is ON in phStaging2. DISCLOSURE — this is a re-file, not a fresh discovery: phlimbo-ea ledger carries this OPEN as V3-L-19 (Low), fingerprint `38aefbfbe6da599fc5250a2cc73125465c845480e34b6a63984b2febae4a053c`, which anticipated this exact situation from the phlimbo side. RE-FILE BASIS: V3-L-19's own `usefulNegativeResults.v3Unwired` field holds the entry at Low on the finding that "PhlimboV3 has ZERO references anywhere in phoenix-phase-2-staging" and that "phStaging pins lib/phlimbo-ea at 6cb0bc0c, a commit whose src/ predates PhlimboV3.sol entirely". Both statements are FALSE at b9391b1: the pin is f279c62 and story 076 deploys both contracts. The prospective leg V3-L-19 explicitly declined to grade is now real, at a different repo, a different entryPoint, and with a new story-faithfulness component. V3-L-19 also carries an unresolved Low-vs-QA severity dispute for human triage; that dispute travels with this entry and must not be silently re-decided.

classification.whyNotMedium: No protocol function is shown to be impacted and no value leaks. Grading an unexercised-pipeline gap as Medium without a demonstrated behavioural difference would be exactly the overstatement the C4 screen rejects.

justification: LOW for THIS deploy-site instance. Two things put it above pure documentation noise at this specific site: it is graded at the moment of a mainnet cutover that CREATEs the contracts, so 'tested bytecode is not deployed bytecode' is a live deploy-gate condition rather than a hypothetical; and the story's Preflight tick is demonstrably false about this repo's own first-party foundry.toml, which is a story-faithfulness deviation independent of any compiler question. It goes no higher: no defect is demonstrated, and the finding's own text correctly refuses to claim one.
